items.title: Urbie Green interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995
items.q: There’s a little Jack Jenny and Billy Butterfield and Artie Shaw in us too I guess.

ctx.x: I wanted to ask you about your personal style of playing the trombone. Who, when you were coming up, who did you listen to? Who did you think was the voice on trombone? And as Monk has referred to, when did you decide that you had a voice?

Well, I think you strive to find your feelings and emotional contact with the music, you know so that makes it individual, no matter who you are. You know if you can really do what’s true to yourself, you know, that’s about as good as you can get I guess. But of course with all the other influences getting you ready for it you know in the meantime. But early voices I guess Trummy Young, Jack Jenny — I never heard a lot of him but he had that solo that was played all around on Artie Shaw’s record of “Stardust”…
He was with Ellington, wasn’t he?
